title: Strings, safely
hints: See 'New syntax': strings end at '\0', snprintf's return value tells you whether it truncated, and <ctype.h> has isspace/toupper.

my_strlen: advance a pointer until it reaches '\0' and return the distance. copy_bounded: ONE snprintf with "%s"; it truncated if the length it wanted is >= cap. count_words: count the spots where a non-space char starts a new word. to_upper: overwrite each char.
Other data, counting digits: `size_t d = 0; for (; *s != '\0'; s++) if (isdigit((unsigned char)*s)) d++;` · For words, carry a `bool in_word` and update it on every char.

Near-answer: `int wanted = snprintf(dst, cap, "%s", src); return wanted < 0 || (size_t)wanted >= cap;` · count_words: `bool space = isspace((unsigned char)*s); if (!space && !in_word) words++; in_word = !space;`
